standing.title: Smorgasburg Prospect Park
standing.address: Breeze Hill, Prospect Park (enter at Lincoln Road), Brooklyn, NY
standing.description: Brooklyn's open-air food market at Breeze Hill in Prospect Park, with dozens of independent vendors. Free to enter; pay per stall.
standing.time_note: Sundays 11am-6pm; arrive before noon to beat the line.
standing.practical_note: Entirely outdoors; check the forecast and bring water in heat.
standing.date_idea_reason: Open-air food market you can graze through together, then walk into Prospect Park.
standing.why_now: Runs every Sunday of the season and pairs naturally with a Prospect Park afternoon.

standing.title: NYC Resistor Public Craft Night
standing.description: Open craft night at the NYC Resistor hacker collective: bring a project, use the space, meet members. Free and open to the public, 18 and over.
standing.time_note: Mondays and Thursdays 6:30-9:30pm. Free, but 18+ only.
standing.practical_note: Fourth-floor walkup; confirm on Eventbrite since craft night is occasionally cancelled for private classes.
standing.date_idea_reason: A free, hands-on makerspace evening is an unusual low-cost date with something to actually do.
standing.why_now: Runs twice a week year-round and is one of the few genuinely free weeknight drop-in activities.

standing.title: Whitney Museum free Friday evening
standing.description: The Whitney is free to all every Friday evening from 5 to 10pm, and also on the second Sunday of each month.
standing.time_note: Free admission Fridays 5-10pm. Free tickets are limited and released in advance.
standing.practical_note: Reserve the free timed ticket ahead; walk-up availability runs out on busy evenings.
standing.date_idea_reason: Free evening museum hours next to the High Line and a dense stretch of bars, so the museum is the anchor rather than the whole plan.
standing.why_now: A standing free window that makes a good anchor for a Friday evening in the Meatpacking District.

standing.title: Queens Night Market
standing.address: Behind the New York Hall of Science, 47-01 111th St, Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Queens, NY 11368
standing.description: Open-air night market behind the New York Hall of Science with about a hundred independent food, art, and merchandise vendors, deliberately kept low-priced.
standing.time_note: Saturdays 4pm to midnight. Note the seasonal gap between late August and mid September.
standing.practical_note: Outdoors and cash-friendly; the adjacent lot charges for parking, so the 7 train is easier.

price.display: Free entry; most dishes capped at a few dollars

standing.date_idea_reason: Cheap, walkable, and genuinely varied: dozens of cuisines in one loop, good for a low-pressure evening.
standing.why_now: Runs every Saturday evening in season; the 7 train to 111th St drops you four blocks away.

standing.title: Whitney Museum free second Sunday
standing.description: The Whitney offers free admission to everyone on the second Sunday of every month.
standing.time_note: Admission is free to all on the second Sunday of each month during normal hours.
standing.why_now: Falls in this window and only comes around once a month.

standing.title: MoMA free Friday evening
standing.description: MoMA offers free admission on Friday evenings. Free tickets are limited, released in advance, and go quickly.
standing.time_note: Free Friday evenings, roughly 4-8pm. Confirm the current window and ticket release on moma.org.
standing.practical_note: Book the free timed ticket the moment it is released; the line for walk-ups is long.
standing.why_now: A standing weekly free window at a museum that is otherwise one of the most expensive in the city.

holiday_plan.intro: For Oct. 10-12, prioritize rail-friendly Hudson Valley plans for Saturday/Sunday and reserve Monday for places explicitly open on the holiday. Do not rely on car-trip timing for the long weekend without rechecking traffic, and book timed-entry/tour slots where venues recommend it.

trips.title: Beacon: Dia Beacon plus an opening-weekend concert
trips.why: Strong car-free art day: Dia Beacon is next to the Metro-North Beacon stop, is open Friday-Monday 10 a.m.-5 p.m., and has Isang Yun: Images at Dia Beacon on Saturday, Oct. 10 at 2 p.m., free with museum admission but with limited seating and separate event registration.
trips.transport: CAR-FREE: Metro-North Hudson Line from Grand Central to Beacon; Dia says trains run hourly during museum hours and the museum is an 8-10 minute walk from Beacon station. CAR-OPTIONAL: Dia lists approximate NYC driving time as 80 minutes in normal conditions.
trips.time_budget: Full day; the venue-sourced walking transfer is 8-10 minutes from Beacon station, plus Hudson Line travel and museum time.
trips.booking_note: Advance Dia reservations are suggested but not required; event seating is limited and registration is separate. Arrive before 4:30 p.m. for admission. On-site parking is limited on busy weekends and holidays.

trips.title: Cold Spring: West Point Foundry Preserve and river-village wandering
trips.why: A low-friction car-free nature/history day: West Point Foundry Preserve is a free, year-round outdoor museum with interpretive trails through a National Historic Landmark industrial site, and Cold Spring’s compact Main Street is walkable from Metro-North.
trips.transport: CAR-FREE: Metro-North Hudson Line to Cold Spring, then walk to the village and preserve area. CAR-OPTIONAL: driving is possible, but parking and holiday traffic should be rechecked.
trips.time_budget: Easy day trip; allow a full day if combining the preserve, riverfront, lunch, and the Putnam History Museum when it is open.
trips.booking_note: The preserve is free and open year-round dawn to dusk. Putnam History Museum is open Wednesday-Sunday 12-4 p.m. during open season, so it fits Oct. 10-11 but not the Monday holiday unless the museum posts a special opening.

trips.title: Hudson and Olana: one-night art, architecture, and river views
trips.destination: Hudson, NY and Olana State Historic Site
trips.why: Best overnight pick: stay in Hudson, use the weekend for galleries/food, and reserve Olana for its 250-acre designed landscape and house tours. Olana’s page specifically notes tours open Monday Oct. 12, while the park is open daily 8 a.m. to sunset.
trips.transport: CAR-FREE WITH LOCAL TRANSFER: Amtrak Empire Service normally serves Hudson, then use taxi/rideshare/local transport to Olana; Amtrak pages were blocked in this research, so exact schedules remain unconfirmed. CAR-OPTIONAL: driving keeps Olana and nearby villages easier, but recheck long-weekend traffic.
trips.time_budget: One night; practical as Sat-Sun or Sun-Mon if tour times and lodging line up.
trips.booking_note: Olana says tours sell out quickly and advanced reservations are strongly recommended. Arrive 30 minutes before any tour and leave 30 minutes between multiple tour experiences.

trips.title: Storm King Art Center: large-scale outdoor sculpture in peak October season
trips.why: A distinctive outdoor art-and-landscape day with enough scale to feel like a real escape. Storm King is open Wednesday-Monday, closed Tuesdays, with October weekend early opening noted on the visit page.
trips.transport: CAR-REQUIRED RECOMMENDED: onsite parking address is 20 Old Pleasant Hill Rd., New Windsor, NY. LIMITED CAR-FREE OPTION UNCONFIRMED: Storm King says Coach USA offers round-trip Port Authority service, but the Coach USA product page fetched as no matching tours, so verify before relying on it.
trips.time_budget: Full day; Storm King’s own transport page says Beacon station is about 30 minutes by car and Salisbury Mills-Cornwall station about 10 minutes by car.
trips.booking_note: Pre-purchased tickets are essential to guarantee admission and parking; onsite tickets may be limited or unavailable for certain time slots. Final entry is 5 p.m.; no overnight parking.

trips.title: Grounds For Sculpture: New Jersey sculpture park and arboretum
trips.why: A closer, highly practical art/nature alternative if Hudson Valley ticketing or weather looks awkward: 42 landscaped acres, 300-plus sculptures, indoor galleries, and year-round programming.
trips.transport: CAR-REQUIRED OR TRANSIT-PLUS-RIDESHARE: drive directly, or use NJ Transit rail planning to Hamilton/nearby stations and arrange the final local transfer. This is not a clean door-to-door car-free option unless the local transfer is preplanned.
trips.time_budget: Half-to-full day; exact rail plus local-transfer time should be checked in NJ Transit trip planner for the chosen departure.
trips.booking_note: Admission tickets are non-refundable but may be rescheduled if capacity allows; tickets are released on a rolling basis. The fetched official pages did not surface holiday-specific hours, so confirm Oct. 10-12 hours before buying.

local_ideas.title: Brooklyn Botanic Garden fall garden day
local_ideas.why: BBG’s October hours list Tuesday-Sunday 10 a.m.-6 p.m. and specifically say it is open Monday Oct. 12, 10 a.m.-6 p.m.; advance tickets are recommended and all visitors need tickets.

local_ideas.title: Dia Chelsea: free Chelsea art stop
local_ideas.why: Dia Chelsea is free, open Wednesday-Saturday 12-6 p.m., and closed Sunday-Monday, so Saturday is the window. It currently lists David Lamelas: The Machine on view and public tours every second Saturday at 1 p.m., with reservations suggested but not required.

local_ideas.title: NYC Columbus Day Parade planning page
local_ideas.why: The Columbus Citizens Foundation’s official page is updated for the 2026 Columbus Day Parade and says they look forward to the parade in 2026, but the fetched page did not provide a confirmed step-off time or route; use it only after checking final details.

local_ideas.title: NYBG Fall-O-Ween as a Bronx fall fallback
local_ideas.why: NYBG’s official Fall-O-Ween page describes seasonal pumpkins, gourds, fall flowers, special weekends, and evening light-trail programming; the fetched page did not expose exact Oct. 10-12 schedule details, so verify admission category and Monday opening before going.

checks: Confirm each venue’s Oct. 10-12 hours the week of travel, especially Monday Oct. 12 holiday exceptions.
For Dia Beacon, register separately for Isang Yun: Images if choosing the Oct. 10 concert; admission alone may not guarantee seating.
For Olana, book house/landscape tours in advance and confirm the Monday Oct. 12 special tour opening on the ticketing page.
For Storm King, pre-purchase timed admission/parking and verify whether the Coach USA package is actually bookable; do not assume a car-free route.
For Hudson/Olana, Amtrak official pages were blocked during research, so verify train schedules directly before treating the overnight as car-free.
For all car trips, recheck same-day traffic because the requested roughly-three-hour radius is normal-traffic only, not a long-weekend guarantee.
For NYC parade or Indigenous Peoples’ Day programming, verify final official route, time, and organizer pages; several city/community pages were blocked or unavailable in this research.
